title: Contract formation — general framework
subject: Contract Law
text: Educational doctrine note: contract-formation analysis commonly considers offer, acceptance, consideration where applicable, intention, capacity, and whether the parties manifested sufficiently definite assent. Apply only the elements supported by the supplied facts.
verification: Verify against the current official law and course materials before relying on this note.

title: Breach — general analytical framework
subject: Contract Law
text: Educational doctrine note: breach analysis asks what obligation was undertaken, whether the relevant performance occurred, whether non-performance is legally excused, and what consequences may follow. Separate factual proof from the legal characterization of the conduct.
verification: Verify the governing statute, contract terms, and current authorities separately.

title: Proportionality — general constitutional reasoning
subject: Constitutional Law
text: Educational doctrine note: proportionality analysis may examine whether a rights-limiting measure pursues a legitimate objective, has a rational connection to that objective, is suitably necessary, and maintains an appropriate balance between competing interests. The precise test depends on the governing jurisdiction and context.
verification: Verify the applicable constitutional provision and current judicial formulation.

title: Criminal liability — elements-first analysis
subject: Criminal Law
text: Educational doctrine note: criminal analysis generally separates the prohibited conduct or act element from the required mental element, then considers causation, defenses, and the applicable burden and standard of proof. Do not infer an element that is absent from the supplied facts.
verification: Verify the current offence definition and procedural rules before relying on this note.

title: Negligence — general framework
subject: Tort Law
text: Educational doctrine note: negligence reasoning commonly considers duty, breach of the applicable standard, factual and legal causation, and legally recognized damage. The content and formulation of each element vary by jurisdiction and claim.
verification: Verify the jurisdiction-specific duty, causation, defenses, and remedy rules.

title: Contract formation — U.S. educational framework
subject: Contract Law
text: Educational doctrine note: a U.S. contract-formation analysis may examine offer, acceptance, consideration, intent, definiteness, and applicable defenses. The governing rules can differ across common law and statutory contexts.
verification: Verify the relevant state or federal authority and current course materials.

title: Criminal liability — U.S. elements-first framework
subject: Criminal Law
text: Educational doctrine note: criminal analysis should identify the precise offence elements, required mental state, causation where relevant, defenses, and the prosecution's applicable burden. The elements depend on the governing jurisdiction and offence.
verification: Verify the governing code, jurisdiction, and current authority.

title: Free-expression analysis — issue spotting
subject: Constitutional Law
text: Educational doctrine note: free-expression problems require identifying the governmental action, protected activity, applicable level of scrutiny or doctrinal test, relevant exceptions, and the facts supporting each element. The exact framework is context dependent.
verification: Verify the applicable constitutional text and current controlling authority.

title: IRAC reasoning discipline
subject: General Legal Reasoning
text: Educational reasoning note: identify one precise issue, state only the rule or test supported by the available sources, connect each material fact to an element, and conclude with the strength and limits of the analysis. Keep assumptions visibly separate from supplied facts.
verification: This is a study aid, not legal authority.
